title: Does FFmpeg -color_range pc convert or only relabel?
fullTitle: FFmpeg -color_range pc: 6.1.1 Relabels Black as 16, 8.1.2 Converts

scenes.narration: Your encode looks washed out: black is gray. Is the video wrong, or only the label? We encode a test card of pure black, pure white and two patches near the ends nine ways with libx264, and read the file on ffmpeg six point one point one and eight point one point two.
captions: Black looks gray after an encode.
The pixels, or only the label? Two builds.

scenes.narration: The card is lossless RGB: black zero, white two fifty five, patches at eight and two forty seven. Reader one is ffprobe plus signalstats. Reader two reads the raw luma byte. A player shows it as is if the tag says full, otherwise it stretches sixteen to two thirty five.

The default, dash pix fmt y u v four twenty p, writes black as luma sixteen and white as two thirty five, with no range tag. That is fine: players stretch sixteen to zero. Dash color range t v changes nothing. Both builds agree.

Now dash color range p c, the same command on two builds. On six point one point one, the raw frame is byte for byte the default: black still sixteen. Only the label changed, so a player shows gray sixteen. On eight point one point two, the pixels are converted: black is zero.

scenes.chapter: Real full range, and a control
scenes.narration: Dash pix fmt y u v j four twenty p, or scale equals out range equals full, gives zero and two fifty five, tagged p c. Control: a stream copy that rewrites only the full range flag. Flag one on limited bytes: black shows sixteen. Flag zero on full bytes: eight and two forty seven are crushed to zero and two fifty five.
Check your build, not your memory: the label and the pixels must match. Use ffprobe and signalstats. Not tested: other builds, real players, real footage, other encoders, ten bit.
captions: Not tested: other builds, real players.
